title: Inverse image of the completed integral twist line, compatibly with coefficient field inclusions
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $h:S'\to S$ a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] let $h^{-1}$ be the inverse image of sheaves along the base-change functor of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; an $R$-module sheaf $M$ gives the $h^{-1}R$-module sheaf $h^{-1}M$. For a finite extension $H/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_H$, uniformizer $\varpi_H$ and $A_{H,n}=\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n$, and for $T\in\{S,S'\}$, let $(B)_T$ denote the constant sheaf of a ring $B$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], let $R_{H,T}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{H,T}=\varprojlim_n(A_{H,n})_T$ be the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and, with the roots of unity $\mu_{\ell^r,T}$ and transitions $u\mapsto u^\ell$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], inverse limits [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] and tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], let
$$\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T=\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^r,T},\qquad \mathcal O_H(1)_T=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}(\mathcal O_H)_T$$
be the integral twist line of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], an $R_{H,T}$-module by clause 3 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. Let $\gamma_{B}:h^{-1}(B)_S\to(B)_{S'}$ be the comparison of constant ring sheaves of a finite ring $B$ [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] and $c^h_{\mu_{\ell^r}}:h^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,S}\to\mu_{\ell^r,S'}$ that of roots of unity [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image]. Then:

1. The ring map $\alpha_{h,H}:h^{-1}R_{H,S}\to R_{H,S'}$ whose composite with the $n$-th projection is $\gamma_{A_{H,n}}\circ h^{-1}(\pi_n)$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings.
2. The map $\tau_h:h^{-1}\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S\to\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_{S'}$ whose composite with the $r$-th projection is $c^h_{\mu_{\ell^r}}\circ h^{-1}(\mathrm{pr}_r)$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves.
3. There is an isomorphism $\rho_{h,H}:h^{-1}\mathcal O_H(1)_S\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_H(1)_{S'}$, semilinear over $\alpha_{h,H}$, which on local sections sends $h^{-1}(t\otimes a)$ to $\tau_h(h^{-1}t)\otimes a$ for $a\in\mathcal O_H$.
4. Let $E\subset F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\iota_{EF}:R_{E,T}\to R_{F,T}$ be the ring map whose composite with the projection to $(A_{F,n})_T$ is the projection to $(A_{E,k})_T$ followed by the map induced by $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_F$, for any $k$ with $\varpi_E^k\mathcal O_F\subseteq\varpi_F^n\mathcal O_F$. Let $j_{EF}:\mathcal O_E(1)_T\to\mathcal O_F(1)_T$ be $t\otimes a\mapsto t\otimes a$. Then $\alpha_{h,F}\circ h^{-1}(\iota_{EF})=\iota_{EF}\circ\alpha_{h,E}$ and $\rho_{h,F}\circ h^{-1}(j_{EF})=j_{EF}\circ\rho_{h,E}$.

proof.text: For each finite extension H and each n, the comparison on the finite quotient A_{H,n} is the canonical constant-ring map gamma_{A_{H,n}}. By det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit, R_{H,T} is canonically the inverse limit of these finite constant sheaves, and by det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-pullback (1), inverse image carries this limit presentation from S to S'. The finite maps in that statement are the constant-section maps of prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map. Therefore the unique map alpha_{h,H} whose n-th projection is gamma_{A_{H,n}} composed with h^{-1}(pi_n) is an isomorphism of rings. Its characterization by all projections also gives compatibility with every quotient transition.

source.place: The integral twist paragraph: inverse-limit presentation and inverse image of the completed coefficient line.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-inverse-image-compatible-free-tower] to the base-change functor $u_h:S_{\mathrm{proet}}\to S'_{\mathrm{proet}}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] (it preserves the final object, fibre products and coverings), to the ring tower $R_r=(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_S$ with its reductions, and to $M_r=\mu_{\ell^r,S}$ with $t_r(u)=u^\ell$, a transition semilinear over the reductions by [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Hypothesis on $\kappa$: Step 1 for $H=\mathbf Q_\ell$ ($\mathcal O_H=\mathbf Z_\ell$, $\varpi=\ell$) says that $\alpha_{h,\mathbf Q_\ell}=(\varprojlim_r\gamma_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r})\circ\kappa$ is an isomorphism, and $\varprojlim_r\gamma_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}$ is an isomorphism because every $\gamma_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}$ is [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]; hence $\kappa$ is an isomorphism. Local bases: [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free] (1), with $\ell$ invertible on $S$, gives a pro-etale cover $\widetilde S\to S$ and $\zeta_r\in\mu_{\ell^r,S}(\widetilde S)$ with $\zeta_{r+1}^\ell=\zeta_r$ such that $a\mapsto\zeta_r^a$ is an isomorphism $(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_{\widetilde S}\to\mu_{\ell^r,\widetilde S}$; by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (1)-(3) the site $\widetilde S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is the localized site $S_{\mathrm{proet}}/\widetilde S$, with $(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_S|_{\widetilde S}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_{\widetilde S}$ and $\mu_{\ell^r,S}|_{\widetilde S}=\mu_{\ell^r,\widetilde S}$ (both have sections $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$-roots on the same objects $V$). So $b_r(a)=\zeta_r^a$ are linear isomorphisms, and $t_rb_{r+1}(a)=\zeta_{r+1}^{\ell a}=\zeta_r^a=b_r(\bar a)$. The tower lemma gives the isomorphism $\theta:h^{-1}\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S\to\varprojlim_rh^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,S}$ whose $r$-th coordinate is $h^{-1}(\mathrm{pr}_r)$, linear over $\kappa$. By [lem-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image-iso] (1) the maps $c^h_{\mu_{\ell^r}}$ form a morphism of inverse systems, so $\varprojlim_rc^h_{\mu_{\ell^r}}$ is defined [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]; each $c^h_{\mu_{\ell^r}}$ is an isomorphism by the first displayed isomorphism of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists] ($\ell$ invertible on $S$ and $S'$), the canonical comparison of roots of unity being the adjoint comparison of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image]. Put $\tau_h=(\varprojlim_rc^h_{\mu_{\ell^r}})\circ\theta$: an isomorphism whose $r$-th projection is $c^h_{\mu_{\ell^r}}\circ h^{-1}(\mathrm{pr}_r)$, and it is the only map with these projections. Semilinearity: $\theta$ is linear over $\kappa$, and $c^h_{\mu_{\ell^r}}$ is semilinear over $c^h_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}$ [lem-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image-iso] (2), which is $\gamma_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}$ by the last clause of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]; so $\tau_h$ is semilinear over $(\varprojlim_r\gamma_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r})\circ\kappa=\alpha_{h,\mathbf Q_\ell}$ for the coordinatewise action of $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}=R_{\mathbf Q_\ell,T}$ on $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T$ of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] (2).

source.place: Roots of unity paragraph and the inverse-limit construction of the integral twist.

proof.text: For a discrete ring $\Lambda\in\{\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_H\}$ (infinite, so [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] does not apply) [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], applied to the geometric morphism of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], gives the ring isomorphism $\delta_\Lambda:h^{-1}\Lambda_S\to\Lambda_{S'}$ carrying constant sections to the same scalars. Two ring maps out of $h^{-1}\Lambda_S$ that agree on the images of constant sections agree, since $\Lambda_S$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $h^{-1}$ is the sheafified colimit construction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; hence $\delta_{\mathcal O_H}$ restricts to $\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$, and the projections of $\alpha_{h,\mathbf Q_\ell}\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon_S)$ and $\epsilon_{S'}\circ\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ to $(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_{S'}$ agree (both send $a$ to $\bar a$), where $\epsilon_T:(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T\to\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}$ is the map of constants through which $(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T$ acts on $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T$. By Step 2, $\tau_h$ is therefore semilinear over $\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$. Since $\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ is an isomorphism, the module pullback $(\mathbf Z_\ell)_{S'}\otimes_{h^{-1}(\mathbf Z_\ell)_S}h^{-1}M$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] (with $c=\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$) is $h^{-1}M$ with its action transported along $\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$, and that lemma gives an isomorphism $h^{-1}(\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_S}(\mathcal O_H)_S)\cong h^{-1}\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S\otimes h^{-1}(\mathcal O_H)_S$, $h^{-1}(t\otimes a)\mapsto h^{-1}t\otimes h^{-1}a$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Compose with $\tau_h\otimes\delta_{\mathcal O_H}$, a tensor product of isomorphisms semilinear over the same isomorphism $\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$; the composite $\rho_{h,H}$ is an isomorphism onto $\mathcal O_H(1)_{S'}$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and sends $h^{-1}(t\otimes a)$ to $\tau_h(h^{-1}t)\otimes a$. Semilinearity over $\alpha_{h,H}$: the $R_{H,T}$-action on $\mathcal O_H(1)_T$ is through the isomorphism $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}(\mathcal O_H)_T\cong R_{H,T}$ of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] (3), $(x\otimes b)\cdot(t\otimes a)=xt\otimes ba$, the canonical map whose $n$-th projection sends $x\otimes b$ to $\mathrm{pr}_k(x)\bar b\in(A_{H,n})_T$ for $\ell^k\mathcal O_H\subseteq\varpi_H^n\mathcal O_H$. After each projection, $\alpha_{h,H}(h^{-1}(x\otimes b))$ and $\alpha_{h,\mathbf Q_\ell}(h^{-1}x)\otimes\delta_{\mathcal O_H}(h^{-1}b)$ both give $\gamma_{A_{H,n}}(h^{-1}(\mathrm{pr}_k(x)\bar b))$, because $\gamma$ is a ring map fixing constants (Step 1). Hence $\rho_{h,H}((x\otimes b)(t\otimes a))=\alpha_{h,\mathbf Q_\ell}(x)\tau_h(t)\otimes ba=\alpha_{h,H}(x\otimes b)\,\rho_{h,H}(t\otimes a)$ on local pure tensors, which generate locally, so $\rho_{h,H}$ is semilinear over $\alpha_{h,H}$.

source.place: The integral twist paragraph: tensoring the roots-of-unity comparison with the coefficient ring.

proof.text: For E contained in F, the inclusions of valuation rings induce compatible maps of the finite quotient towers A_{E,k} to A_{F,n}; the condition varpi_E^k O_F contained in varpi_F^n O_F is exactly what makes the map at level n well defined. The maps iota_{EF} are therefore the induced maps between the inverse limits in Step 1. Naturality for homomorphisms of ring towers in lem-pur-inverse-image-compatible-free-tower, together with the defining constant-section naturality in prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map, gives alpha_{h,F} composed with h^{-1}(iota_{EF}) equal to iota_{EF} composed with alpha_{h,E}. The equality can be checked after every finite projection, where it is the same inclusion of residue rings.

source.place: The integral twist paragraph and the coefficient-field compatibility used in the final base-change sentence.

proof.text: The maps j_{EF} are obtained by tensoring the identity on Z_ell(1)_T with the inclusion of constant coefficient rings. Apply the naturality clause for compatible semilinear morphisms of module towers in lem-pur-inverse-image-compatible-free-tower to the tower maps defining j_{EF}; together with the formula for rho in Step 3, both composites carry h^{-1}(t tensor a) to tau_h(h^{-1}t) tensor a. Hence rho_{h,F} composed with h^{-1}(j_{EF}) equals j_{EF} composed with rho_{h,E}. This also shows that the two compatibilities are independent of the chosen local generators, since all maps are induced by the universal tensor and inverse-limit constructions.
